rows.title: Stromness distillery
rows.source_title: List of whisky distilleries in Scotland
rows.evidence: Wikipedia's list of former malt distilleries gives the row Stromness, location Orkney, region Highland, year closed 1928, demolished 1940. The Orkney article says Stromness is on the Mainland, and that Kirkwall and Stromness are on that island. Wikidata Q2356880 is at 58.9578,-3.3021, the town of Stromness.
rows.summary: The former malt distilleries table lists Stromness with the location Orkney and records that it closed in 1928 and was demolished in 1940. Stromness on the Mainland is the second-largest settlement in Orkney. Both of Orkney's burghs, Kirkwall and Stromness, are on this island.

rows.title: Orkney distillery
rows.source_title: List of whisky distilleries in Scotland
rows.evidence: The June 2026 operating malt table names Orkney at Kirkwall, Island region. The Orkney article places Kirkwall on the Mainland. The Island single malt page also lists Orkney distillery on Orkney, under distilleries in development, so this row is medium rather than high.
rows.summary: As of June 2026, there are 154 whisky distilleries operating in Scotland. The malt whisky table lists Orkney with the location Kirkwall, in the Island region, founded in 2018. Both of Orkney's burghs, Kirkwall and Stromness, are on this island.

rows.title: North Uist distillery
rows.source_title: List of whisky distilleries in Scotland
rows.evidence: The operating malt table lists North Uist separately from Benbecula distillery, with the location cell Benbecula. Benbecula is the atlas island of that name. There is no separate prose article.
rows.summary: As of June 2026, there are 154 whisky distilleries operating in Scotland. The malt whisky table lists North Uist with the location Benbecula, in the Island region, founded in 2024.

rows.title: Isle of Wight Distillery
rows.source_title: List of whisky distilleries in England
rows.evidence: The England whisky-distillery article says the Isle of Wight Distillery started distilling whisky in December 2015 and released a whisky in December 2018. Its table gives the town as Ryde, the port town on the Isle of Wight.
rows.summary: The Isle of Wight Distillery is known for their gin and vodka brand Mermaid, but also started distilling whisky in December 2015. The first whisky was released in December 2018. The active-distillery table gives the town as Ryde.

rows.title: Wight Distillery
rows.source_title: List of whisky distilleries in England
rows.evidence: The England list's town cell for Wight Distillery is Isle of Wight, distinct from the 2015 Isle of Wight Distillery row at Ryde. The first-release year is 2027, so this row is filed as not yet releasing whisky.
rows.summary: The active independent distilleries table lists Wight Distillery, established in 2023, with a first release in 2027, and gives the town as Isle of Wight.

rows.title: Scilly Isles Distillery
rows.source_title: List of whisky distilleries in England
rows.evidence: The England whisky list names Scilly Isles Distillery at St Mary's, first release 2024. The name Scilly Isles distinguishes this St Mary's from the other St Mary's islands in the atlas. The atlas id is scilly-st-marys, St Mary's (Isles of Scilly).
rows.summary: As of 2026 are currently 35 distilleries across England with whisky available to purchase. The active-distillery table names Scilly Isles Distillery, established in 2019, with a first release in 2024, and gives the town as St Mary's.

rows.title: Illicit stills on Skye
rows.evidence: The Talisker distillery article places seven registered distilleries and many illicit operations on Skye. It does not name the other five registered stills, so they are not separate rows.
rows.summary: At its peak, Skye had seven registered distilleries and many illicit operations. Talisker is one of only two, alongside Torabhaig Distillery, as of 2026.

rows.title: Saxa Vord distillery
rows.evidence: The Saxa Vord article places a gin distillery on Unst and says the Shetland Reel single malts were sourced from Glenglassagh, with casks brought to the island. The June 2026 operating list also names Saxa Vord at Unst, but the distillery article contradicts that it is a whisky still.
rows.reject_reason: The distillery's own article says it is a gin distillery. Its whiskies were sourced from another distillery, and as of 2022 the proposed whisky still had not been funded.
rows.summary: Saxa Vord distillery is a gin distillery on the island of Unst, Shetland. In 2018, the company announced a fundraising drive to raise £4.5 million in order to construct a proposed single malt whisky distillery at the site, next to the existing gin distillery. As of 2022, the company had not successfully raised the funds to begin whisky production. In September 2015, they released the first Shetland Reel branded whiskies: a set of four single malts sourced from Glenglassagh distillery.

rows.title: Blackwood distillery
rows.evidence: The Blackwood article says the Unst construction was never completed. A stalled plan, and the spirit was distilled elsewhere.
rows.reject_reason: The whisky distillery proposed for Unst was never built. The gins were contract distilled in London, and the brand later moved to Inverkip.
rows.summary: Initially, the whisky distillery was proposed for a location at Catfirth, near South Nesting. However, in April 2006, Blackwood announced alternative plans to convert part of the disused RAF Saxa Vord base on Unst to distillery usage. The construction on Unst would never be completed, and the site would later become Saxa Vord distillery. The gins from this time period were contract distilled in London.

rows.title: Achill Island Distillery
rows.evidence: County Mayo includes the mainland as well as Achill. No fetched Wikipedia sentence places the still on the island.
rows.reject_reason: The page names Achill Island Distillery in County Mayo and does not say the still is on Achill. The Achill Island article does not mention a distillery.
rows.summary: Achill Island Distillery, County Mayo (est. 2015) – produces the Irish American brand whiskey. The list of whiskey distilleries in Ireland gives the location as County Mayo.

rows.title: Lambay Island whiskey
rows.evidence: Lambay Island's whiskey section says production is in Ireland, with maturation of some batches on the island, and that an on-island micro-distillery was only approved in principle.
rows.reject_reason: The whiskey is produced in Ireland and only matured on the island. A micro-distillery had planning permission approved in principle, which is not a still the page places on the island.
rows.summary: The whiskey is produced in Ireland, with water added from one of the island's Trinity Well, and some batches are matured on the island. Application for planning permission for a micro-distillery for whiskey and gin, for small batch production in spring and autumn when the island's water supply is strongest, was made in 2019, and approved in principle, subject to clarification around waste disposal.

rows.title: Freeport distillery
rows.evidence: Islay single malts lists Freeport among closed distilleries and says the location is unknown.
rows.reject_reason: The closed-distillery list says the location is unknown.

rows.title: Scarabus distillery
rows.evidence: Islay single malts includes Scarabus in the closed list and states there is no evidence of production.
rows.reject_reason: The page lists Scarabus among closed names and says there is no evidence of production.

rows.title: Gartbreck distillery
rows.evidence: Islay single malts says the Gartbreck project was stalled. The June 2026 operating list does not include it.
rows.reject_reason: The page says the project was stalled as of December 2018. It is not in the June 2026 list of operating distilleries.
rows.summary: A new distillery at Gartbreck Farm, just south of Bowmore, was planned in 2014, but as of December 2018 the project was stalled over a land and management dispute.

rows.title: ManX Spirit
rows.evidence: Manx Spirit is made on the Isle of Man by redistilling Scotch. The page says it cannot legally be sold as whisky.
rows.reject_reason: The page says this is a redistillation of Scottish whiskies and that the result cannot legally be sold in the United Kingdom labelled as whisky.
rows.summary: ManX Spirit is a clear spirit, 40% alcohol by volume, produced by redistillation of existing Scottish whiskies, resulting in a clear and colourless product. A United Kingdom High Court case concluded that the redistillation process and lack of colour meant that the drink could not legally be sold in the United Kingdom while labeled as whisky.

rows.title: Colonsay gin
rows.evidence: Colonsay's article places gin production on the island and does not describe a whisky still. One of the gins was first distilled off the island.
rows.reject_reason: The island article describes gin, not a whisky still.
rows.summary: In 2016 the brewery launched a gin, called Wild Island Botanic Gin, distilled with hand-gathered wild botanicals from the island. Initially distilled off the island, production moved to Colonsay in 2018.
